sentences.text: Applicant :- Kamal Singh Kushwaha

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Imran Ullah,Rahul Kumar Jadaun Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.
Counter affidavit filed by the State as well as supplementary affidavit filed by the learned counsel for the applicant are taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail during the trial in Case Crime No.535 of 2018, under sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of the I.P.C.
and Section 3 & 7 of Essential Commodities Act, Police Station-Jalaun, District -Jalaun.
Contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the instant matter due to ulterior motive.

He next added that as per prosecution story while using the E-Pos Machine, applicant in collusion with the fair price shop dealers has committed black-marketing of the foodgrains, though the police has failed to collect the cogent piece of evidence against him.

He submits that, in fact, the admitted position is that password is provided by the Supply Inspector, but the E-Pos Machine is used by the different fair price shop dealers at Kamal Singh Kushwaha vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154047907/
1 various place of distribution of the foodgrains, though, the password is been given in the morning and E-Pos Machine which are operated by the fair price shop dealers throughout whole-day and the same always remain in the possession of the fair price shop dealers and, as such, the offence, if any,
has been committed by the fair price shop dealers and not by the Supply Inspector.

sentences.text: He added that the foodgrains of PDS Scheme are distributed as per unit of the Rashion Card and that is responsibility of fair price shop dealers concerned and the applicant had no involvement in the same and he is unaware about any offence committed behind his back.

He also added that the departmental enquiry is conducted by the District Magistrate, wherein it was found that there is negligence on the part of the applicant and, thus no criminal liability can be attributed to the applicant as the criminal intent is missing.

He next added that there is no cogent piece of evidence against the applicant so as to connect him and the co-accused persons namely, Shiva Chaurasiya,
Sagar Chaurasiya and Mahendra Saravagi @ Raju have already been enlarged on bail by co-ordinate Benches of this Court vide orders dated 28.03.2019, 23.03.2019 and 28.03.2019 in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application Nos.12466, 37405 and 12507 of 2019, respectively.

sentences.text: He next submits that applicant has criminal history of 12 cases, which he has explained in para 66 of the bail application and he is languishing in jail since 05-07-2024.
He submits that the applicant is a government employee and he undertakes that in case, he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty of the same and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.

Per contra, learned AGA appearing for the State has opposed the contentions aforesaid and submits that there are serious allegations against the applicant and he is involved in committing the offence as applicant in collusion with the fair price dealers, has committed black-marketing while providing his password.

He also added that password is always in the knowledge of the applicant and it is impossible that without allowing the password to be used, the entries could not have been feeded and after an enquiry instituted by the District Magistrate, it was also borne out that applicant was involved in blackmarketing and, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.
Having heard learned counsels for the parties and after perusal of material placed on record, it transpires that applicant is a government employee and he is languishing in jail since 05-07-2024.

This Court has also taken note of fact that E-Pos Machine is used by the fair price shop dealers and the password is provided by the Supply Inspector for all the entries throughout the days and it prima facie seems that it is not possible for a Supply Inspector to supervise at one point of time to all the E-Pos machines on various places of his given region; co-accused persons have already been enlarged on bail and applicant has criminal history of 12 cases, which has been explained coupled with the fact that applicant has undertaken that if he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty of the same and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel of both sides, nature of accusation and severity of punishment in case of conviction, nature of supporting evidence, prima facie satisfaction of the Court in support of the charge, reformative theory of punishment and considering larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and, without expressing any view on the merits of the case,
I find it to be a fit case of bail.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant-Kamal Singh Kushwaha involved in the aforementioned crime be released on bail,
on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned, with the following conditions:-
(1) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/
pressurizing the witnesses, or otherwise during the investigation or trial;
(2) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
He shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;
(3) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.; and (4) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
It is clarified that the observations made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of this bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the merits of the case.

Order Date :- 13.9.2024 Ashutosh  Kamal Singh Kushwaha vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154047907/
